name_en: Hie-zushi — millet and wild boar simmered into a porridge for the long winter
summary_ja: 猪の骨付き肉を湯がいた出汁に、米や稗、野菜を入れて炊く椎葉村の雑炊。縄文以前から食べられてきたとされる雑穀・稗を使い、猪をさばいた際には村中に振る舞われる冬の栄養源として伝わってきた。
summary_en: Wild boar bones are simmered into a broth, then rice, millet, and vegetables are added and cooked down into a porridge — a Shiiba village dish built on millet, a grain said to have been eaten in Japan since before rice farming; whenever a boar was dressed, the porridge it made was shared around the whole village to see out the long winter.
source_title: 稗ずーしー／稗がゆ 宮崎県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Toukibi meshi — rice cooked with cracked, wind-dried corn kernels
summary_ja: 軒下で寒風にさらして乾燥させたとうもろこしを踏み臼でひき割りにし、米に混ぜて炊く高千穂地方の飯。米が貴重だった時代にかさ増しの役目を果たしたとされ、冷めると囲炉裏で焼いて食べたと伝わる。
summary_en: Corn, dried under the eaves through the winter wind, is cracked in a foot-powered mortar and cooked into the rice — a dish from the Takachiho area said to have stretched scarce rice further; once cold, it was grilled over the hearth fire to bring it back.
source_title: とうきびめし 宮崎県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Miyazaki torimeshi — rice cooked with chicken, burdock, and carrot, a farmhand's field meal
summary_ja: 細く切った鶏肉とごぼう、人参、しいたけを炒めて出汁で煮つけ、米と一緒に炊きあげる宮崎の飯料理。稲刈りや畑仕事の合間におにぎりとして食べられてきた農家飯で、新富町では「春日ずし」の別名でも知られる。
summary_en: Thinly sliced chicken, burdock, carrot, and shiitake are stir-fried and simmered in dashi, then cooked into the rice — a Miyazaki farmhand's meal once carried into the fields as rice balls during harvest, known in Shintomi town by another name, Kasuga-zushi.
source_title: とりめし 宮崎県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省
